doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Thanking donors and the Fillius Jazz Archive
summary: The conversation turns to arts depending on donations and Stripling thanks the archive's supporters.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: It also pays, you must have been presenting quality entertainment over the years, you know.

Yes, we have. And you know the band has been in existence about 47, 48 years, we’ll be celebrating our 50th soon. But that’s what we’re supposed to do. That’s a given. But it also, you have to thank people, you have to acknowledge their gift to you because most people don’t know, and I’ll stop yacking my tongue now but most people don’t know that the arts are sustained through donations. I mean that’s why, I forgot, the first thing you said to me, and I realized they were important, was when you introduced me is this is the something something Hamilton College, what are those people’s —
Right. Those people are why you and I sit here.

And so I think it’s important to acknowledge that you know, and thank you. You’re supposed to do that, but I know that you do that from your heart too, that that’s real. And it’s real to me and that’s why I wanted to have you say their name one more time because I don’t forget that.
